1	# VariantRail
2	
3	VariantRail is a small backend for a genome variant annotation pipeline with a
4	reproducible provenance trail. It ingests a VCF subset, filters records by
5	quality and depth, annotates every ALT allele with a built-in gene/consequence
6	table, summarises the result, and records one SHA-256 link per pipeline step so
7	any run can be re-derived and checked byte for byte.
8	
9	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
10	
11	- a sample is VCF text that is parsed and validated at upload time;
12	- a run replays four fixed steps: `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate`, `summarize`;
13	- each step stores the hash of its input, the hash of its output, and the
14	  previous link's hash, so the trail is a chain;
15	- hashes depend only on content and parameters, never on the sample id, the
16	  run id, wall-clock time, or process state;
17	- the annotation table is built in and its content hash is itself a
18	  provenance input;
19	- every output variant keeps the original VCF line verbatim.
20	
21	## Requirements
22	
23	- Python 3.11 or newer
24	- no third-party runtime dependencies
25	
26	## Run the service
27	
28	```bash
29	PYTHONPATH=src python -m variantrail.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18083 --database variantrail.db
30	```
31	
32	The process prints `VariantRail listening on http://127.0.0.1:18083` after it
33	has bound the port.
34	
35	## HTTP API
36	
37	All request and response bodies are JSON except the `jsonl`, `tsv` and `vcf`
38	run export endpoints, and unknown fields are rejected. Both `POST` endpoints
39	require an `Idempotency-Key` header; repeating a key returns the stored first
40	response verbatim, and reusing a key for another operation is a `conflict`.
41	
42	### Health
43	
44	`GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
45	
46	### Create a sample
47	
48	```http
49	POST /samples
50	Idempotency-Key: sample-1
51	Content-Type: application/json
52	
53	{"id":"trio-1","vcf":"##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n##reference=GRCh38\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\nchr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr1\t11856378\trs2\tG\tT\t20\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tGA\t50\tPASS\tDP=31\nchr17\t43093445\t.\tC\tT\t99\tPASS\tDP=55\n"}
54	```
55	
56	Returns HTTP 201 with a deterministic projection of the parsed sample:
57	
58	```json
59	{"chromosomes":["chr1","chr7","chr17"],"id":"trio-1","meta_lines":2,"records":4,
60	 "sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef"}
61	```
62	
63	`sha256` is the SHA-256 of the uploaded VCF text. `id` must match
64	`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}` and is unique (`conflict` otherwise).
65	
66	### The supported VCF subset
67	
68	The text is split on `\n`; one trailing newline is optional and a single
69	trailing `\r` per line is ignored, so CRLF files are accepted. Every violation
70	raises `validation_error` with a message shaped `line <n>: ...`.
71	
72	1. The first line must be `##fileformat=VCFv4.<digits>`.
73	2. Zero or more `##key=value` meta lines follow, `key` matching
74	   `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` and `value` non-empty.
75	3. Exactly one `#CHROM` line follows whose tab-separated columns are exactly
76	   `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO`. `FORMAT` and sample columns are
77	   not supported and are rejected.
78	4. One or more data lines follow, each with exactly 8 tab-separated fields:
79	   - `CHROM` matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; chromosome blocks must be contiguous, so
80	     a chromosome may not reappear once another chromosome started;
81	   - `POS` is a positive integer and non-decreasing within a chromosome, and
82	     `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)` is unique in the file;
83	   - `ID` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a value without whitespace, `;` or `,`;
84	   - `REF` is a non-empty `[ACGTN]+` sequence;
85	   - `ALT` is one or more `[ACGTN]+` sequences separated by `,` without
86	     repeats; symbolic alleles such as `<DEL>` or `*` are rejected;
87	   - `REF` and `ALT` are upper-cased before storage;
88	   - `QUAL` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a non-negative decimal number;
89	   - `FILTER` is `.` (empty list), `PASS`, or `;`-separated tokens matching
90	     `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; `PASS` must not be combined with another token;
91	   - `INFO` is `.` (empty object) or `;`-separated `KEY` / `KEY=VALUE` entries
92	     with `KEY` matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`, no repeated keys and a
93	     non-empty whitespace-free value; `DP`, when present, must be a
94	     non-negative integer.
95	
96	Blank lines, header lines after the first data record, a missing `#CHROM`
97	header, and a file with no data records are rejected.
98	
99	### Start a run
100	
101	```http
102	POST /samples/trio-1/runs
103	Idempotency-Key: run-1
104	Content-Type: application/json
105	
106	{"id":"run-1","params":{"min_qual":30,"min_dp":10,"pass_only":true,"genes":["MTHFR","EGFR","BRCA1"]}}
107	```
108	
109	`params` is optional; the body must contain `id` and may contain only `params`
110	besides it. The run executes synchronously, so a returned run is always
111	`succeeded`. Returns HTTP 201:
112	
113	```json
114	{"id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1",
115	 "sample_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
116	 "params":{"genes":["BRCA1","EGFR","MTHFR"],"impacts":[],"min_dp":10,"min_qual":30.0,"pass_only":true},
117	 "status":"succeeded","provenance_length":4,
118	 "provenance_head":"40807a2cebf5110a5a3be231ab78ca690823b9def8414dd373314354cac65b40",
119	 "statistics":{"records_total":4,"records_kept":3,"records_filtered":1,
120	   "filter_counts":{"allele_filtered":0,"dp_below_min":0,"not_pass":0,"qual_below_min":1},
121	   "alleles_total":4,"alleles_kept":3,
122	   "consequence_counts":{"frameshift_variant":1,"missense_variant":1,"stop_gained":1},
123	   "impact_counts":{"HIGH":2,"MODERATE":1},
124	   "gene_counts":{"BRCA1":1,"EGFR":1,"MTHFR":1}}}
125	```
126	
127	### Run parameters
128	
129	Every key is optional; the stored `params` object always contains all five
130	core keys, plus `record_filter` only when one was supplied. `genes` and
131	`impacts` are stored sorted, so request order never changes a hash.
132	
133	- `pass_only` (boolean, default `false`) — keep only records whose `FILTER` is
134	  exactly `["PASS"]`.
135	- `min_qual` (non-negative finite number, default `0.0`, stored as a float) —
136	  keep records with `QUAL >= min_qual`.
137	- `min_dp` (non-negative integer, default `0`) — keep records with
138	  `DP >= min_dp`.
139	- `genes` (array of non-empty strings, default `[]` = no restriction) — after
140	  annotation keep only alleles whose gene is listed. An allele with no table
141	  match has gene `null` and is dropped when `genes` is non-empty.
142	- `impacts` (array, default `[]` = no restriction) — after annotation keep only
143	  alleles whose impact is listed; values must come from `HIGH`, `MODERATE`,
144	  `LOW`, `MODIFIER`, `UNKNOWN`.
145	- `record_filter` (expression object, optional) — a structured, nested
146	  record-level predicate applied after `pass_only`, `min_qual` and `min_dp` and
147	  before the gene/impact allowlists. When omitted the stored `params` object
148	  holds only the other five keys and the run is byte-for-byte identical to an
149	  older run; when present it is stored, normalized, under `record_filter`.
150	
151	A record that passed the record-level filters but whose alleles are all removed
152	by `genes`/`impacts` is dropped as well.
153	
154	### Record filter expressions
155	
156	Every expression node is either a logical node or a condition object; mixing
157	both forms in one node is rejected:
158	
159	- `{"all":[<expr>, ...]}` — true when every child is true; the array is
160	  non-empty.
161	- `{"any":[<expr>, ...]}` — true when at least one child is true; the array is
162	  non-empty.
163	- `{"not":<expr>}` — true when the single child expression is false.
164	- `{"field":"<field>","op":"<op>","value":<value>}` — a condition; `value` is
165	  required for every op except `exists`, which must omit it.
166	
167	`field` is one of `chrom`, `pos`, `id`, `ref`, `alt`, `qual`, `dp`, `filter`
168	or `info.<KEY>` (any INFO key). `op` is one of:
169	
170	- `eq` — direct scalar comparison. For `alt` and `filter` the condition is
171	  true when any element equals the value.
172	- `in` — `value` must be a non-empty array; true on membership. For `alt` and
173	  `filter` it is true when any record element appears in the array.
174	- `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte` — numeric ordering; `value` must be a number and
175	  the field must be `pos`, `qual`, `dp`, or an `info.<KEY>` whose stored value
176	  parses fully to a finite decimal number.
177	- `exists` — takes no `value`; true when the field is present and non-null. An
178	  INFO bare flag counts as present.
179	
180	A missing field, a `null` value (`ID`/`QUAL` `.`), or an INFO value that does
181	not parse as a finite decimal makes every op other than `exists` false; wrap
182	such a condition in `not` to test for absence. The stored expression is
183	normalized (`in` arrays are sorted, numeric values stored as floats), so
184	equivalent submissions hash identically. Expressions may nest at most 16
185	levels. Any unknown field or op, malformed node, empty `all`/`any`,
186	field/op type mismatch, `exists` with a `value`, another op without one, or
187	nesting beyond 16 levels makes run creation return 400 `validation_error`
188	without saving the run or the idempotency response.
189	
190	### Filter accounting and statistics
191	
192	`filter_counts` attributes every filtered record to exactly one reason, in this
193	precedence: `not_pass` (`pass_only` set and `FILTER` is not `["PASS"]`);
194	`qual_below_min` (`QUAL` below `min_qual`, or `null` while `min_qual > 0`);
195	`dp_below_min` (`DP` below `min_dp`, or `null` while `min_dp > 0`);
196	`rule_mismatch` (a `record_filter` was supplied and its expression evaluated
197	false for the record — present in the run statistics and annotate-step counts,
198	even when zero); `allele_filtered` (survived the record-level filters but no
199	allele survived the allowlists). Hence
200	`records_filtered == sum(filter_counts.values())` and
201	`records_kept == records_total - records_filtered` always hold.
202	
203	`alleles_total` counts every ALT allele of every record and `alleles_kept`
204	counts the alleles present in the run's variants. `gene_counts` uses the key
205	`NA` for alleles with no table match. `consequence_counts`, `impact_counts` and
206	`gene_counts` omit zero counts and are sorted by key.
207	
208	### Get a run
209	
210	`GET /runs/run-1` returns the run document shown above.
211	
212	### Get run variants
213	
214	`GET /runs/run-1/variants` returns `{"count":<n>,"run_id":"run-1","variants":[...]}`
215	in file order. Each variant repeats the parsed fields plus `raw`, the original
216	line, so every output stays traceable to the input:
217	
218	```json
219	{"alts":["A"],
220	 "annotations":[{"allele":"A","allele_index":1,"consequence":"missense_variant","gene":"MTHFR","impact":"MODERATE"}],
221	 "chrom":"chr1","dp":42,"filter":["PASS"],"id":"rs1","info":{"DP":"42"},"line":4,
222	 "pos":11856378,"qual":60.0,"raw":"chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42","ref":"G"}
223	```
224	
225	`line` is the 1-based line of the record in the uploaded VCF and `allele_index`
226	is the 1-based VCF ALT index.
227	
228	### Get run quality control
229	
230	`GET /runs/run-1/qc` summarizes only the run's already-stored variants and
231	metadata: filtering and annotation are not re-executed, no data is rewritten,
232	and the run, its variants, its exports and its provenance are unchanged. No
233	`Idempotency-Key` is required. Returns HTTP 200:
234	
235	```json
236	{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...",
237	 "provenance_head":"...",
238	 "records":{"total":7,"pass":6,"missing_qual":1,"missing_dp":1,"multiallelic":1,
239	   "qual":{"count":6,"min":20.0,"max":99.0},
240	   "dp":{"count":6,"min":5,"max":60}},
241	 "alleles":{"total":8,"snv":7,"mnv":0,"insertion":1,"deletion":0,
242	   "transitions":4,"transversions":3,"non_acgt_snv":0,"ti_tv_ratio":1.3333333333333333}}
243	```
244	
245	`records` is scoped to retained records (one entry per stored variant):
246	
247	- `total` is the number of retained records;
248	- `pass` counts only records whose `FILTER` is exactly the single value `PASS`;
249	- `missing_qual` and `missing_dp` count records whose `QUAL` / `DP` is `null`;
250	- `multiallelic` counts records carrying at least two retained annotations;
251	- `qual` and `dp` each give `count`, `min` and `max` over non-null values;
252	  when no value is non-null they are `{"count":0,"min":null,"max":null}`.
253	
254	`alleles.total` counts every retained annotation. Each allele falls into
255	exactly one class using only the lengths of `REF` and `annotation.allele`:
256	
257	- `snv` — both are one base long;
258	- `mnv` — equal length greater than one;
259	- `insertion` — the ALT is longer;
260	- `deletion` — the ALT is shorter.
261	
262	For SNVs whose two bases are both in `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`, `A↔G` and `C↔T`
263	pairs count as `transitions` and every other pair as `transversions`. An SNV
264	involving `N` counts as `non_acgt_snv` and enters neither total. `ti_tv_ratio`
265	is `transitions / transversions` as a JSON number, or `null` when
266	`transversions` is zero. Every count is present even when zero.
267	
268	A run with no retained variants still returns 200 with all counts zero, the
269	`QUAL`/`DP` bounds and `ti_tv_ratio` null. An unknown `run_id` returns 404
270	`not_found` with the message `run <run_id> was not found`. Repeated requests
271	for the same run return byte-identical JSON.
272	
273	### Export run results
274	
275	`GET /runs/run-1/exports/jsonl`, `GET /runs/run-1/exports/tsv` and
276	`GET /runs/run-1/exports/vcf` hand the
277	retained variants of a saved run to downstream analysis as a stable payload.
278	The body is generated on demand from the stored run; it is never written to
279	disk, and the run, its variants and its provenance are not modified.
280	
281	`jsonl` is served as `application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`: one variant object
282	per line in the original file order, using the same fields and values as
283	`GET /runs/{run_id}/variants`. Each line is UTF-8 JSON with no indentation and
284	keys sorted lexicographically, terminated by a single LF; the body ends with
285	the last line's LF (no trailing blank line). A run with no variants returns an
286	empty body.
287	
288	`tsv` is served as `text/tab-separated-values; charset=utf-8` and always opens
289	with the fixed header:
290	
291	```
292	chrom	pos	id	ref	alt	allele_index	gene	consequence	impact	qual	dp	filter	info	line
293	```
294	
295	Each retained annotation is one row, so a record with several retained ALT
296	alleles spans several rows; variant file order and annotation order are kept.
297	Formatting rules:
298	
299	- `id`, `gene`, `qual` or `dp` is `NA` when null; `qual` otherwise keeps the
300	  JSON decimal form (e.g. `60.0`);
301	- an empty `FILTER` is `.`; several filters are joined with `;`;
302	- `INFO` is `;`-joined `KEY=VALUE` pairs sorted by key; bare flags are written
303	  as `KEY`; empty INFO is `.`;
304	- numbers use the JSON decimal representation and text is not quoted.
305	
306	A run with no variants returns just the header line. An unknown `run_id`
307	returns 404 `not_found`; any `format` other than `jsonl`, `tsv` or `vcf`
308	returns 400 `validation_error`, both with the standard error object.
309	
310	`vcf` is served as `text/x-variant-call-format; charset=utf-8`: the retained
311	variants rendered back as VCF v4.2 text (UTF-8, LF line endings). The header
312	opens with `##fileformat=VCFv4.2`, repeats the uploaded sample's other meta
313	lines in their original order, adds `##source=variantrail`, and declares four
314	export INFO keys — `ALLELE_INDEX` (Integer), `VT_GENE`, `VT_CONSEQUENCE` and
315	`VT_IMPACT` (String, all `Number=1`) — before the tab-separated
316	`#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO` column header. Each retained ALT
317	allele is one record, in variant file order and `allele_index` order, with
318	`ALT` holding only the current allele. `ID`, `QUAL` and an empty `FILTER` are
319	`.` when missing; `INFO` lists the original entries sorted by key, then the
320	four export keys (`VT_GENE` is `NA` when no gene is annotated). If an original
321	INFO field uses `ALLELE_INDEX` or one of the `VT_*` keys, the export returns
322	400 `validation_error` naming the conflicting key. A run with no variants
323	returns just the header, and repeated requests are byte-identical.
324	
325	### Compare two runs
326	
327	`GET /runs/{run_id}/compare/{other_run_id}` compares the retained ALT alleles
328	of two finished runs — `run_id` on the left, `other_run_id` on the right. It
329	only reads the stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and neither run,
330	its variants, its exports, nor its provenance is modified. The runs may belong
331	to different samples. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.
332	
333	An allele's identity is the tuple `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the
334	same identity within one run count once. Returns HTTP 200:
335	
336	```json
337	{"left":{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
338	 "right":{"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
339	 "counts":{"shared":4,"left_only":4,"right_only":0,"union":8},
340	 "shared":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"T",
341	   "gene":"MTHFR","consequence":"stop_gained","impact":"HIGH"}],
342	 "left_only":[...],
343	 "right_only":[...],
344	 "gene_summary":{"MTHFR":{"shared":1,"left_only":1,"right_only":0}},
345	 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"shared":4,"left_only":0,"right_only":0}}}
346	```
347	
348	- `shared`, `left_only` and `right_only` hold every distinct allele on both
349	  sides, on the left only, and on the right only; each element carries
350	  `chrom`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt`, `gene`, `consequence` and `impact`, with
351	  `gene` kept as JSON `null` when the allele has no table match. Comparing a
352	  run with itself puts every allele in `shared`.
353	- Each array is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then
354	  `ref`, then `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
355	- `counts` mirrors the three array lengths plus `union`, their total.
356	- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` count the alleles of each bucket per
357	  gene and per impact; keys are sorted lexicographically, a `null` gene
358	  appears as `NA`, and impacts keep their original values.
359	
360	An unknown `run_id` or `other_run_id` returns 404 `not_found` with the
361	message `run <run_id> was not found`.
362	
363	### Compare a cohort of runs
364	
365	`GET /runs/{run_id}/cohort/{other_run_ids}` compares the retained ALT alleles
366	of two or more finished runs at once. `other_run_ids` is two or more run ids
367	joined with commas; the path order (the path `run_id` first, then the comma
368	list) is the cohort queue order. Like the two-run comparison it only reads the
369	stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and no run, variant, export or
370	provenance record is modified. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.
371	
372	An allele's identity is again `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the same
373	identity within one run count once, and annotations are taken as stored — no
374	filtering or re-annotation happens. Returns HTTP 200:
375	
376	```json
377	{"run_count":3,
378	 "runs":[{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
379	         {"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
380	         {"run_id":"run-3","sample_id":"trio-2","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":3}],
381	 "alleles":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"A","gene":"MTHFR",
382	   "consequence":"missense_variant","impact":"MODERATE","run_count":2,
383	   "present_in":["run-1","run-3"]}],
384	 "counts":{"unique_alleles":9,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":3,
385	   "private_alleles":{"run-1":3,"run-2":1,"run-3":0}},
386	 "frequency_summary":{"1":4,"2":3,"3":2},
387	 "gene_summary":{"BRCA1":{"unique_alleles":1,"core_alleles":1,"variable_alleles":0},
388	                "MTHFR":{"unique_alleles":2,"core_alleles":0,"variable_alleles":2}},
389	 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"unique_alleles":4,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":2}}}
390	```
391	
392	- `runs` repeats the queued runs in queue order; each entry has `run_id`,
393	  `sample_id`, `sample_sha256` and `allele_count`, the number of distinct
394	  retained alleles in that run.
395	- `alleles` holds every distinct allele of the union (different ALTs at the
396	  same coordinate are separate entries). Each element carries `chrom`, `pos`,
397	  `ref`, `alt`, `gene` (`null` when the allele has no table match),
398	  `consequence`, `impact`, `run_count` — the number of cohort runs containing
399	  it — and `present_in`, the run ids of those runs in queue order. The array
400	  is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then `ref`, then
401	  `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
402	- `counts.unique_alleles` is the total number of entries in `alleles`;
403	  `core_alleles` counts alleles present in all `run_count` runs,
404	  `variable_alleles` alleles present in between 2 and `run_count - 1` runs,
405	  and `private_alleles` breaks the alleles present in exactly one run down by
406	  `run_id`, in queue order (runs without a private allele show `0`).
407	- `frequency_summary` has the string keys `"1"` through
408	  `"<run_count>"` and counts alleles present in exactly that many runs, with
409	  missing frequencies filled in as `0`.
410	- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` group `unique_alleles`, `core_alleles`
411	  and `variable_alleles` per gene and per impact; a `null` gene appears as
412	  `NA`, categories with no alleles are omitted, and keys are sorted
413	  lexicographically. Private alleles are not separately listed there
414	  (`unique = core + variable + private`).
415	
416	Changing the queue order returns the same data apart from the order of `runs`
417	and of each `present_in`; the allele set, counts and summaries are unchanged,
418	and repeating a request is byte-identical.
419	
420	Fewer than two run ids in the path is a 400 `validation_error` with the
421	message `cohort requires at least two distinct runs`; a repeated run id is a
422	409 `conflict` with the message `cohort run ids must be distinct`; any run id
423	that does not exist is a 404 `not_found` with the message
424	`run <run_id> was not found`.
425	
426	### The annotation table
427	
428	Annotation matches the exact tuple `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)`. A variant with no
429	matching row is annotated `gene: null`, `consequence: "intergenic_variant"`,
430	`impact: "MODIFIER"`.
431	
432	```
433	chr1  11856378  G  A    MTHFR  missense_variant       MODERATE
434	chr1  11856378  G  T    MTHFR  stop_gained            HIGH
435	chr7  55019017  G  GA   EGFR   frameshift_variant     HIGH
436	chr7  55019017  G  T    EGFR   stop_gained            HIGH
437	chr7  55273000  C  T    EGFR   synonymous_variant     LOW
438	chr11 5227002   T  C    HBB    missense_variant       MODERATE
439	chr12 25245350  C  A    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
440	chr12 25245350  C  T    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
441	chr12 25245351  C  T    KRAS   splice_donor_variant   HIGH
442	chr17 43093445  C  T    BRCA1  stop_gained            HIGH
443	chr17 43093446  A  G    BRCA1  missense_variant       MODERATE
444	chr17 7676154   C  T    TP53   missense_variant       MODERATE
445	chr19 11200138  C  T    LDLR   missense_variant       MODERATE
446	chrX  31137345  A  G    DMD    missense_variant       MODERATE
447	```
448	
449	This is a small synthetic table with GRCh38-style chromosome names and real gene
450	symbols; the coordinates are illustrative and it is not a clinical annotation
451	source.
452	
453	### Get run provenance
454	
455	`GET /runs/run-1/provenance` returns `{"run_id","verified","chain_verified",
456	"reproduction_verified","head_sha256","steps":[...]}`, where a step looks like:
457	
458	```json
459	{"step":1,"name":"ingest","params":{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"},
460	 "input_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
461	 "output_sha256":"0f5d73dd61762cefc2df233d1e604de50d21df017a6f9e5608851a3c700c6103",
462	 "previous_sha256":null,
463	 "hash":"6de42193fc25e82afb9c32b0d6170629b69eb25268d978864f9162b27ed75530"}
464	```
465	
466	Write `canonical(x)` for `json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",",":"),
467	sort_keys=True)` and `H(x)` for the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the UTF-8
468	bytes of `canonical(x)`. The four links are:
469	
470	| step | name | params | input_sha256 | output_sha256 |
471	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
472	| 1 | `ingest` | `{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"}` | SHA-256 of the VCF text | `H({"records":<parsed records>})` |
473	| 2 | `filter` | `min_dp`, `min_qual`, `pass_only`, plus the normalized `record_filter` when supplied | step 1 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<record-reason keys>,"records":<kept records>})` |
474	| 3 | `annotate` | `annotation_table_sha256`, `genes`, `impacts` | step 2 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<record keys plus allele_filtered>,"variants":<variants>})` |
475	| 4 | `summarize` | `{}` | step 3 `output_sha256` | `H(<statistics>)` |
476	
477	Without a `record_filter` the step-2 filter counts hold the three original
478	record-reason keys and the step params hold only `min_dp`, `min_qual` and
479	`pass_only`, so every link hash is unchanged from the five-parameter contract.
480	With one, `rule_mismatch` is added (after `dp_below_min`) and the normalized
481	expression is part of the step-2 params; reproduction re-runs the saved
482	expression and the rule result, statistics, variants and all four step output
483	hashes feed the existing `verified` verdict.
484	
485	Each link's own hash covers the previous link, so the trail is tamper-evident:
486	
487	```
488	body = {step, name, params, input_sha256, output_sha256, previous_sha256}
489	hash = H(body)                 # previous_sha256 is null for step 1
490	```
491	
492	`chain_verified` recomputes every link hash and checks that each
493	`previous_sha256` equals the previous link's `hash`. `reproduction_verified`
494	re-reads the stored sample VCF, re-executes all four steps with the stored
495	`params`, and compares the four `output_sha256` values, the statistics and the
496	variants. `verified` is the conjunction of both; the endpoint never rewrites the
497	stored trail.
498	
499	## Step-level lineage manifest
500	
501	`variantrail.pipeline.execute(parsed, vcf_text, params)` — the analysis entry
502	used in-process, e.g. `execute(parse_vcf(vcf_text), vcf_text,
503	normalize_params(raw))` — takes an optional `lineage` boolean. When it is
504	omitted or false the return value is exactly the documented
505	`{"filter_counts","provenance","statistics","variants"}` and every behaviour
506	above is unchanged. With `lineage=True` the result adds a self-contained
507	`lineage` object, so a caller can tell from the return value alone — without
508	logs or files — which input, parameters and intermediate steps produced it:
509	
510	```json
511	{"input_sha256":"<SHA-256 of the VCF text>",
512	 "params":{<isolated snapshot of every run parameter as it was at the call>},
513	 "steps":[{"name":"ingest","params":{...},"input_sha256":"...","output_sha256":"...",
514	           "previous_sha256":"0000...0000","sha256":"..."},
515	          ...],
516	 "final_sha256":"..."}
517	```
518	
519	- `params` is a deep snapshot taken before any step runs; mutating the
520	  caller's parameter objects afterwards never changes the returned manifest.
521	  Equivalent dictionaries (keys in a different order) yield the same digests,
522	  since all hashing uses the same canonical JSON, `sort_keys=True`, as the
523	  provenance links.
524	- `steps` lists the steps in their real execution order. A step that actually
525	  executed is always recorded — including on an empty input or when filtering
526	  removes every record — while a step skipped by a condition never appears as
527	  an executed record. The four records are `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate` and
528	  `summarize`; `params`, `input_sha256` and `output_sha256` are the values
529	  actually used by that step.
530	- The first record's `previous_sha256` is fixed at 64 zeroes. Each record's
531	  `sha256` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (UTF-8) of all its other
532	  fields — `name`, `params`, `input_sha256`, `output_sha256` and
533	  `previous_sha256`; object keys sort by Unicode code point, array order is
534	  kept, and numbers, booleans and `null` stay their JSON types.
535	- `final_sha256` is the final chain summary: the same construction one level
536	  up, sealing `input_sha256`, `params` and all `steps`. The manifest is fully
537	  deterministic — the same input content, equivalent parameters and the same
538	  step outputs produce a byte-for-byte identical manifest on repeated runs;
539	  changing any input, parameter or step output changes every digest from the
540	  first affected record onward.
541	
542	`variantrail.verify_lineage(lineage)` is the matching public entry point: it
543	recomputes every record digest, the record-to-record linkage and the chain
544	head, and re-seals the manifest, returning `True` only when everything is
545	consistent. A tampered field, reordered or missing record, wrong head value or
546	mismatched `final_sha256` returns `False`, and the passed object is never
547	modified. Malformed input — not an object, a missing or unknown field, or a
548	digest that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters — raises `ValueError`.
549	
550	A non-boolean `lineage` argument raises `TypeError`. When lineage is enabled,
551	a parameter value that cannot be represented as JSON (such as a set or a
552	custom object) raises `TypeError` as well, before any pipeline step executes.
553	The HTTP API does not expose this option: its bodies are JSON already, the
554	request contract (exactly `id` and optional `params`) and every other command
555	line and error behaviour are unchanged.
556	
557	## Errors
558	
559	```json
560	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"line 5: POS must be a positive integer"}}
561	```
562	
563	Validation errors return 400, missing resources 404, conflicts 409. A missing
564	`Idempotency-Key` header is a `validation_error`, and reusing one key for a
565	different operation is a `conflict`.
566	
567	## Tests
568	
569	```bash
570	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
571	```
572

# VariantRail

VariantRail is a small backend for a genome variant annotation pipeline with a
reproducible provenance trail. It ingests a VCF subset, filters records by
quality and depth, annotates every ALT allele with a built-in gene/consequence
table, summarises the result, and records one SHA-256 link per pipeline step so
any run can be re-derived and checked byte for byte.

The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:

- a sample is VCF text that is parsed and validated at upload time;
- a run replays four fixed steps: `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate`, `summarize`;
- each step stores the hash of its input, the hash of its output, and the
  previous link's hash, so the trail is a chain;
- hashes depend only on content and parameters, never on the sample id, the
  run id, wall-clock time, or process state;
- the annotation table is built in and its content hash is itself a
  provenance input;
- every output variant keeps the original VCF line verbatim.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m variantrail.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18083 --database variantrail.db
```

The process prints `VariantRail listening on http://127.0.0.1:18083` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON except the `jsonl`, `tsv` and `vcf`
run export endpoints, and unknown fields are rejected. Both `POST` endpoints
require an `Idempotency-Key` header; repeating a key returns the stored first
response verbatim, and reusing a key for another operation is a `conflict`.

### Health

`GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a sample

```http
POST /samples
Idempotency-Key: sample-1
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"trio-1","vcf":"##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n##reference=GRCh38\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\nchr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr1\t11856378\trs2\tG\tT\t20\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tGA\t50\tPASS\tDP=31\nchr17\t43093445\t.\tC\tT\t99\tPASS\tDP=55\n"}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with a deterministic projection of the parsed sample:

```json
{"chromosomes":["chr1","chr7","chr17"],"id":"trio-1","meta_lines":2,"records":4,
 "sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef"}
```

`sha256` is the SHA-256 of the uploaded VCF text. `id` must match
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}` and is unique (`conflict` otherwise).

### The supported VCF subset

The text is split on `\n`; one trailing newline is optional and a single
trailing `\r` per line is ignored, so CRLF files are accepted. Every violation
raises `validation_error` with a message shaped `line <n>: ...`.

1. The first line must be `##fileformat=VCFv4.<digits>`.
2. Zero or more `##key=value` meta lines follow, `key` matching
   `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` and `value` non-empty.
3. Exactly one `#CHROM` line follows whose tab-separated columns are exactly
   `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO`. `FORMAT` and sample columns are
   not supported and are rejected.
4. One or more data lines follow, each with exactly 8 tab-separated fields:
   - `CHROM` matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; chromosome blocks must be contiguous, so
     a chromosome may not reappear once another chromosome started;
   - `POS` is a positive integer and non-decreasing within a chromosome, and
     `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)` is unique in the file;
   - `ID` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a value without whitespace, `;` or `,`;
   - `REF` is a non-empty `[ACGTN]+` sequence;
   - `ALT` is one or more `[ACGTN]+` sequences separated by `,` without
     repeats; symbolic alleles such as `<DEL>` or `*` are rejected;
   - `REF` and `ALT` are upper-cased before storage;
   - `QUAL` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a non-negative decimal number;
   - `FILTER` is `.` (empty list), `PASS`, or `;`-separated tokens matching
     `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; `PASS` must not be combined with another token;
   - `INFO` is `.` (empty object) or `;`-separated `KEY` / `KEY=VALUE` entries
     with `KEY` matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`, no repeated keys and a
     non-empty whitespace-free value; `DP`, when present, must be a
     non-negative integer.

Blank lines, header lines after the first data record, a missing `#CHROM`
header, and a file with no data records are rejected.

### Start a run

```http
POST /samples/trio-1/runs
Idempotency-Key: run-1
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"run-1","params":{"min_qual":30,"min_dp":10,"pass_only":true,"genes":["MTHFR","EGFR","BRCA1"]}}
```

`params` is optional; the body must contain `id` and may contain only `params`
besides it. The run executes synchronously, so a returned run is always
`succeeded`. Returns HTTP 201:

```json
{"id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1",
 "sample_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
 "params":{"genes":["BRCA1","EGFR","MTHFR"],"impacts":[],"min_dp":10,"min_qual":30.0,"pass_only":true},
 "status":"succeeded","provenance_length":4,
 "provenance_head":"40807a2cebf5110a5a3be231ab78ca690823b9def8414dd373314354cac65b40",
 "statistics":{"records_total":4,"records_kept":3,"records_filtered":1,
   "filter_counts":{"allele_filtered":0,"dp_below_min":0,"not_pass":0,"qual_below_min":1},
   "alleles_total":4,"alleles_kept":3,
   "consequence_counts":{"frameshift_variant":1,"missense_variant":1,"stop_gained":1},
   "impact_counts":{"HIGH":2,"MODERATE":1},
   "gene_counts":{"BRCA1":1,"EGFR":1,"MTHFR":1}}}
```

### Run parameters

Every key is optional; the stored `params` object always contains all five
core keys, plus `record_filter` only when one was supplied. `genes` and
`impacts` are stored sorted, so request order never changes a hash.

- `pass_only` (boolean, default `false`) — keep only records whose `FILTER` is
  exactly `["PASS"]`.
- `min_qual` (non-negative finite number, default `0.0`, stored as a float) —
  keep records with `QUAL >= min_qual`.
- `min_dp` (non-negative integer, default `0`) — keep records with
  `DP >= min_dp`.
- `genes` (array of non-empty strings, default `[]` = no restriction) — after
  annotation keep only alleles whose gene is listed. An allele with no table
  match has gene `null` and is dropped when `genes` is non-empty.
- `impacts` (array, default `[]` = no restriction) — after annotation keep only
  alleles whose impact is listed; values must come from `HIGH`, `MODERATE`,
  `LOW`, `MODIFIER`, `UNKNOWN`.
- `record_filter` (expression object, optional) — a structured, nested
  record-level predicate applied after `pass_only`, `min_qual` and `min_dp` and
  before the gene/impact allowlists. When omitted the stored `params` object
  holds only the other five keys and the run is byte-for-byte identical to an
  older run; when present it is stored, normalized, under `record_filter`.

A record that passed the record-level filters but whose alleles are all removed
by `genes`/`impacts` is dropped as well.

### Record filter expressions

Every expression node is either a logical node or a condition object; mixing
both forms in one node is rejected:

- `{"all":[<expr>, ...]}` — true when every child is true; the array is
  non-empty.
- `{"any":[<expr>, ...]}` — true when at least one child is true; the array is
  non-empty.
- `{"not":<expr>}` — true when the single child expression is false.
- `{"field":"<field>","op":"<op>","value":<value>}` — a condition; `value` is
  required for every op except `exists`, which must omit it.

`field` is one of `chrom`, `pos`, `id`, `ref`, `alt`, `qual`, `dp`, `filter`
or `info.<KEY>` (any INFO key). `op` is one of:

- `eq` — direct scalar comparison. For `alt` and `filter` the condition is
  true when any element equals the value.
- `in` — `value` must be a non-empty array; true on membership. For `alt` and
  `filter` it is true when any record element appears in the array.
- `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte` — numeric ordering; `value` must be a number and
  the field must be `pos`, `qual`, `dp`, or an `info.<KEY>` whose stored value
  parses fully to a finite decimal number.
- `exists` — takes no `value`; true when the field is present and non-null. An
  INFO bare flag counts as present.

A missing field, a `null` value (`ID`/`QUAL` `.`), or an INFO value that does
not parse as a finite decimal makes every op other than `exists` false; wrap
such a condition in `not` to test for absence. The stored expression is
normalized (`in` arrays are sorted, numeric values stored as floats), so
equivalent submissions hash identically. Expressions may nest at most 16
levels. Any unknown field or op, malformed node, empty `all`/`any`,
field/op type mismatch, `exists` with a `value`, another op without one, or
nesting beyond 16 levels makes run creation return 400 `validation_error`
without saving the run or the idempotency response.

### Filter accounting and statistics

`filter_counts` attributes every filtered record to exactly one reason, in this
precedence: `not_pass` (`pass_only` set and `FILTER` is not `["PASS"]`);
`qual_below_min` (`QUAL` below `min_qual`, or `null` while `min_qual > 0`);
`dp_below_min` (`DP` below `min_dp`, or `null` while `min_dp > 0`);
`rule_mismatch` (a `record_filter` was supplied and its expression evaluated
false for the record — present in the run statistics and annotate-step counts,
even when zero); `allele_filtered` (survived the record-level filters but no
allele survived the allowlists). Hence
`records_filtered == sum(filter_counts.values())` and
`records_kept == records_total - records_filtered` always hold.

`alleles_total` counts every ALT allele of every record and `alleles_kept`
counts the alleles present in the run's variants. `gene_counts` uses the key
`NA` for alleles with no table match. `consequence_counts`, `impact_counts` and
`gene_counts` omit zero counts and are sorted by key.

### Get a run

`GET /runs/run-1` returns the run document shown above.

### Get run variants

`GET /runs/run-1/variants` returns `{"count":<n>,"run_id":"run-1","variants":[...]}`
in file order. Each variant repeats the parsed fields plus `raw`, the original
line, so every output stays traceable to the input:

```json
{"alts":["A"],
 "annotations":[{"allele":"A","allele_index":1,"consequence":"missense_variant","gene":"MTHFR","impact":"MODERATE"}],
 "chrom":"chr1","dp":42,"filter":["PASS"],"id":"rs1","info":{"DP":"42"},"line":4,
 "pos":11856378,"qual":60.0,"raw":"chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42","ref":"G"}
```

`line` is the 1-based line of the record in the uploaded VCF and `allele_index`
is the 1-based VCF ALT index.

### Get run quality control

`GET /runs/run-1/qc` summarizes only the run's already-stored variants and
metadata: filtering and annotation are not re-executed, no data is rewritten,
and the run, its variants, its exports and its provenance are unchanged. No
`Idempotency-Key` is required. Returns HTTP 200:

```json
{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...",
 "provenance_head":"...",
 "records":{"total":7,"pass":6,"missing_qual":1,"missing_dp":1,"multiallelic":1,
   "qual":{"count":6,"min":20.0,"max":99.0},
   "dp":{"count":6,"min":5,"max":60}},
 "alleles":{"total":8,"snv":7,"mnv":0,"insertion":1,"deletion":0,
   "transitions":4,"transversions":3,"non_acgt_snv":0,"ti_tv_ratio":1.3333333333333333}}
```

`records` is scoped to retained records (one entry per stored variant):

- `total` is the number of retained records;
- `pass` counts only records whose `FILTER` is exactly the single value `PASS`;
- `missing_qual` and `missing_dp` count records whose `QUAL` / `DP` is `null`;
- `multiallelic` counts records carrying at least two retained annotations;
- `qual` and `dp` each give `count`, `min` and `max` over non-null values;
  when no value is non-null they are `{"count":0,"min":null,"max":null}`.

`alleles.total` counts every retained annotation. Each allele falls into
exactly one class using only the lengths of `REF` and `annotation.allele`:

- `snv` — both are one base long;
- `mnv` — equal length greater than one;
- `insertion` — the ALT is longer;
- `deletion` — the ALT is shorter.

For SNVs whose two bases are both in `A`, `C`, `G`, `T`, `A↔G` and `C↔T`
pairs count as `transitions` and every other pair as `transversions`. An SNV
involving `N` counts as `non_acgt_snv` and enters neither total. `ti_tv_ratio`
is `transitions / transversions` as a JSON number, or `null` when
`transversions` is zero. Every count is present even when zero.

A run with no retained variants still returns 200 with all counts zero, the
`QUAL`/`DP` bounds and `ti_tv_ratio` null. An unknown `run_id` returns 404
`not_found` with the message `run <run_id> was not found`. Repeated requests
for the same run return byte-identical JSON.

### Export run results

`GET /runs/run-1/exports/jsonl`, `GET /runs/run-1/exports/tsv` and
`GET /runs/run-1/exports/vcf` hand the
retained variants of a saved run to downstream analysis as a stable payload.
The body is generated on demand from the stored run; it is never written to
disk, and the run, its variants and its provenance are not modified.

`jsonl` is served as `application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`: one variant object
per line in the original file order, using the same fields and values as
`GET /runs/{run_id}/variants`. Each line is UTF-8 JSON with no indentation and
keys sorted lexicographically, terminated by a single LF; the body ends with
the last line's LF (no trailing blank line). A run with no variants returns an
empty body.

`tsv` is served as `text/tab-separated-values; charset=utf-8` and always opens
with the fixed header:

```
chrom	pos	id	ref	alt	allele_index	gene	consequence	impact	qual	dp	filter	info	line
```

Each retained annotation is one row, so a record with several retained ALT
alleles spans several rows; variant file order and annotation order are kept.
Formatting rules:

- `id`, `gene`, `qual` or `dp` is `NA` when null; `qual` otherwise keeps the
  JSON decimal form (e.g. `60.0`);
- an empty `FILTER` is `.`; several filters are joined with `;`;
- `INFO` is `;`-joined `KEY=VALUE` pairs sorted by key; bare flags are written
  as `KEY`; empty INFO is `.`;
- numbers use the JSON decimal representation and text is not quoted.

A run with no variants returns just the header line. An unknown `run_id`
returns 404 `not_found`; any `format` other than `jsonl`, `tsv` or `vcf`
returns 400 `validation_error`, both with the standard error object.

`vcf` is served as `text/x-variant-call-format; charset=utf-8`: the retained
variants rendered back as VCF v4.2 text (UTF-8, LF line endings). The header
opens with `##fileformat=VCFv4.2`, repeats the uploaded sample's other meta
lines in their original order, adds `##source=variantrail`, and declares four
export INFO keys — `ALLELE_INDEX` (Integer), `VT_GENE`, `VT_CONSEQUENCE` and
`VT_IMPACT` (String, all `Number=1`) — before the tab-separated
`#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO` column header. Each retained ALT
allele is one record, in variant file order and `allele_index` order, with
`ALT` holding only the current allele. `ID`, `QUAL` and an empty `FILTER` are
`.` when missing; `INFO` lists the original entries sorted by key, then the
four export keys (`VT_GENE` is `NA` when no gene is annotated). If an original
INFO field uses `ALLELE_INDEX` or one of the `VT_*` keys, the export returns
400 `validation_error` naming the conflicting key. A run with no variants
returns just the header, and repeated requests are byte-identical.

### Compare two runs

`GET /runs/{run_id}/compare/{other_run_id}` compares the retained ALT alleles
of two finished runs — `run_id` on the left, `other_run_id` on the right. It
only reads the stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and neither run,
its variants, its exports, nor its provenance is modified. The runs may belong
to different samples. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.

An allele's identity is the tuple `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the
same identity within one run count once. Returns HTTP 200:

```json
{"left":{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
 "right":{"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
 "counts":{"shared":4,"left_only":4,"right_only":0,"union":8},
 "shared":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"T",
   "gene":"MTHFR","consequence":"stop_gained","impact":"HIGH"}],
 "left_only":[...],
 "right_only":[...],
 "gene_summary":{"MTHFR":{"shared":1,"left_only":1,"right_only":0}},
 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"shared":4,"left_only":0,"right_only":0}}}
```

- `shared`, `left_only` and `right_only` hold every distinct allele on both
  sides, on the left only, and on the right only; each element carries
  `chrom`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt`, `gene`, `consequence` and `impact`, with
  `gene` kept as JSON `null` when the allele has no table match. Comparing a
  run with itself puts every allele in `shared`.
- Each array is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then
  `ref`, then `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
- `counts` mirrors the three array lengths plus `union`, their total.
- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` count the alleles of each bucket per
  gene and per impact; keys are sorted lexicographically, a `null` gene
  appears as `NA`, and impacts keep their original values.

An unknown `run_id` or `other_run_id` returns 404 `not_found` with the
message `run <run_id> was not found`.

### Compare a cohort of runs

`GET /runs/{run_id}/cohort/{other_run_ids}` compares the retained ALT alleles
of two or more finished runs at once. `other_run_ids` is two or more run ids
joined with commas; the path order (the path `run_id` first, then the comma
list) is the cohort queue order. Like the two-run comparison it only reads the
stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and no run, variant, export or
provenance record is modified. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.

An allele's identity is again `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the same
identity within one run count once, and annotations are taken as stored — no
filtering or re-annotation happens. Returns HTTP 200:

```json
{"run_count":3,
 "runs":[{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
         {"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
         {"run_id":"run-3","sample_id":"trio-2","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":3}],
 "alleles":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"A","gene":"MTHFR",
   "consequence":"missense_variant","impact":"MODERATE","run_count":2,
   "present_in":["run-1","run-3"]}],
 "counts":{"unique_alleles":9,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":3,
   "private_alleles":{"run-1":3,"run-2":1,"run-3":0}},
 "frequency_summary":{"1":4,"2":3,"3":2},
 "gene_summary":{"BRCA1":{"unique_alleles":1,"core_alleles":1,"variable_alleles":0},
                "MTHFR":{"unique_alleles":2,"core_alleles":0,"variable_alleles":2}},
 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"unique_alleles":4,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":2}}}
```

- `runs` repeats the queued runs in queue order; each entry has `run_id`,
  `sample_id`, `sample_sha256` and `allele_count`, the number of distinct
  retained alleles in that run.
- `alleles` holds every distinct allele of the union (different ALTs at the
  same coordinate are separate entries). Each element carries `chrom`, `pos`,
  `ref`, `alt`, `gene` (`null` when the allele has no table match),
  `consequence`, `impact`, `run_count` — the number of cohort runs containing
  it — and `present_in`, the run ids of those runs in queue order. The array
  is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then `ref`, then
  `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
- `counts.unique_alleles` is the total number of entries in `alleles`;
  `core_alleles` counts alleles present in all `run_count` runs,
  `variable_alleles` alleles present in between 2 and `run_count - 1` runs,
  and `private_alleles` breaks the alleles present in exactly one run down by
  `run_id`, in queue order (runs without a private allele show `0`).
- `frequency_summary` has the string keys `"1"` through
  `"<run_count>"` and counts alleles present in exactly that many runs, with
  missing frequencies filled in as `0`.
- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` group `unique_alleles`, `core_alleles`
  and `variable_alleles` per gene and per impact; a `null` gene appears as
  `NA`, categories with no alleles are omitted, and keys are sorted
  lexicographically. Private alleles are not separately listed there
  (`unique = core + variable + private`).

Changing the queue order returns the same data apart from the order of `runs`
and of each `present_in`; the allele set, counts and summaries are unchanged,
and repeating a request is byte-identical.

Fewer than two run ids in the path is a 400 `validation_error` with the
message `cohort requires at least two distinct runs`; a repeated run id is a
409 `conflict` with the message `cohort run ids must be distinct`; any run id
that does not exist is a 404 `not_found` with the message
`run <run_id> was not found`.

### The annotation table

Annotation matches the exact tuple `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)`. A variant with no
matching row is annotated `gene: null`, `consequence: "intergenic_variant"`,
`impact: "MODIFIER"`.

```

chr1  11856378  G  T    MTHFR  stop_gained            HIGH
chr7  55019017  G  GA   EGFR   frameshift_variant     HIGH
chr7  55019017  G  T    EGFR   stop_gained            HIGH
chr7  55273000  C  T    EGFR   synonymous_variant     LOW
chr11 5227002   T  C    HBB    missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245350  C  A    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245350  C  T    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245351  C  T    KRAS   splice_donor_variant   HIGH
chr17 43093445  C  T    BRCA1  stop_gained            HIGH
chr17 43093446  A  G    BRCA1  missense_variant       MODERATE
chr17 7676154   C  T    TP53   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr19 11200138  C  T    LDLR   missense_variant       MODERATE
chrX  31137345  A  G    DMD    missense_variant       MODERATE
```

This is a small synthetic table with GRCh38-style chromosome names and real gene
symbols; the coordinates are illustrative and it is not a clinical annotation
source.

### Get run provenance

`GET /runs/run-1/provenance` returns `{"run_id","verified","chain_verified",
"reproduction_verified","head_sha256","steps":[...]}`, where a step looks like:

```json
{"step":1,"name":"ingest","params":{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"},
 "input_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
 "output_sha256":"0f5d73dd61762cefc2df233d1e604de50d21df017a6f9e5608851a3c700c6103",
 "previous_sha256":null,
 "hash":"6de42193fc25e82afb9c32b0d6170629b69eb25268d978864f9162b27ed75530"}
```

Write `canonical(x)` for `json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",",":"),
sort_keys=True)` and `H(x)` for the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the UTF-8
bytes of `canonical(x)`. The four links are:

| step | name | params | input_sha256 | output_sha256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ingest` | `{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"}` | SHA-256 of the VCF text | `H({"records":<parsed records>})` |
| 2 | `filter` | `min_dp`, `min_qual`, `pass_only`, plus the normalized `record_filter` when supplied | step 1 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<record-reason keys>,"records":<kept records>})` |
| 3 | `annotate` | `annotation_table_sha256`, `genes`, `impacts` | step 2 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<record keys plus allele_filtered>,"variants":<variants>})` |
| 4 | `summarize` | `{}` | step 3 `output_sha256` | `H(<statistics>)` |

Without a `record_filter` the step-2 filter counts hold the three original
record-reason keys and the step params hold only `min_dp`, `min_qual` and
`pass_only`, so every link hash is unchanged from the five-parameter contract.
With one, `rule_mismatch` is added (after `dp_below_min`) and the normalized
expression is part of the step-2 params; reproduction re-runs the saved
expression and the rule result, statistics, variants and all four step output
hashes feed the existing `verified` verdict.

Each link's own hash covers the previous link, so the trail is tamper-evident:

```
body = {step, name, params, input_sha256, output_sha256, previous_sha256}
hash = H(body)                 # previous_sha256 is null for step 1
```

`chain_verified` recomputes every link hash and checks that each
`previous_sha256` equals the previous link's `hash`. `reproduction_verified`
re-reads the stored sample VCF, re-executes all four steps with the stored
`params`, and compares the four `output_sha256` values, the statistics and the
variants. `verified` is the conjunction of both; the endpoint never rewrites the
stored trail.

## Step-level lineage manifest

`variantrail.pipeline.execute(parsed, vcf_text, params)` — the analysis entry
used in-process, e.g. `execute(parse_vcf(vcf_text), vcf_text,
normalize_params(raw))` — takes an optional `lineage` boolean. When it is
omitted or false the return value is exactly the documented
`{"filter_counts","provenance","statistics","variants"}` and every behaviour
above is unchanged. With `lineage=True` the result adds a self-contained
`lineage` object, so a caller can tell from the return value alone — without
logs or files — which input, parameters and intermediate steps produced it:

```json
{"input_sha256":"<SHA-256 of the VCF text>",
 "params":{<isolated snapshot of every run parameter as it was at the call>},
 "steps":[{"name":"ingest","params":{...},"input_sha256":"...","output_sha256":"...",
           "previous_sha256":"0000...0000","sha256":"..."},
          ...],
 "final_sha256":"..."}
```

- `params` is a deep snapshot taken before any step runs; mutating the
  caller's parameter objects afterwards never changes the returned manifest.
  Equivalent dictionaries (keys in a different order) yield the same digests,
  since all hashing uses the same canonical JSON, `sort_keys=True`, as the
  provenance links.
- `steps` lists the steps in their real execution order. A step that actually
  executed is always recorded — including on an empty input or when filtering
  removes every record — while a step skipped by a condition never appears as
  an executed record. The four records are `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate` and
  `summarize`; `params`, `input_sha256` and `output_sha256` are the values
  actually used by that step.
- The first record's `previous_sha256` is fixed at 64 zeroes. Each record's
  `sha256` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (UTF-8) of all its other
  fields — `name`, `params`, `input_sha256`, `output_sha256` and
  `previous_sha256`; object keys sort by Unicode code point, array order is
  kept, and numbers, booleans and `null` stay their JSON types.
- `final_sha256` is the final chain summary: the same construction one level
  up, sealing `input_sha256`, `params` and all `steps`. The manifest is fully
  deterministic — the same input content, equivalent parameters and the same
  step outputs produce a byte-for-byte identical manifest on repeated runs;
  changing any input, parameter or step output changes every digest from the
  first affected record onward.

`variantrail.verify_lineage(lineage)` is the matching public entry point: it
recomputes every record digest, the record-to-record linkage and the chain
head, and re-seals the manifest, returning `True` only when everything is
consistent. A tampered field, reordered or missing record, wrong head value or
mismatched `final_sha256` returns `False`, and the passed object is never
modified. Malformed input — not an object, a missing or unknown field, or a
digest that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters — raises `ValueError`.

A non-boolean `lineage` argument raises `TypeError`. When lineage is enabled,
a parameter value that cannot be represented as JSON (such as a set or a
custom object) raises `TypeError` as well, before any pipeline step executes.
The HTTP API does not expose this option: its bodies are JSON already, the
request contract (exactly `id` and optional `params`) and every other command
line and error behaviour are unchanged.

## Errors

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"line 5: POS must be a positive integer"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources 404, conflicts 409. A missing
`Idempotency-Key` header is a `validation_error`, and reusing one key for a
different operation is a `conflict`.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from .errors import ValidationError

_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}$")


def identifier(value: Any, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _IDENTIFIER.match(value):
        raise ValidationError(
            f"{field} must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{{0,99}}"
        )
    return value


def sample_view(document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Public projection of a stored sample; no timestamps, fully deterministic."""
    return {
        "chromosomes": list(document["chromosomes"]),
        "id": document["id"],
        "meta_lines": len(document["meta"]),
        "records": len(document["records"]),
        "sha256": document["sha256"],
    }


def run_view(document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Public projection of a stored run."""
    provenance = document["provenance"]
    return {
        "id": document["id"],
        "params": document["params"],
        "provenance_head": provenance[-1]["hash"],
        "provenance_length": len(provenance),
        "sample_id": document["sample_id"],
        "sample_sha256": document["sample_sha256"],
        "statistics": document["statistics"],
        "status": "succeeded",
    }

7	STEP_FIELDS = ("step", "name", "params", "input_sha256", "output_sha256", "previous_sha256")
8	
9	
10	def canonical(value: Any) -> str:
11	    """Stable JSON rendering: sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace."""
12	    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
13	
14	
15	def digest(value: Any) -> str:
16	    """SHA-256 of the canonical JSON rendering of ``value``."""
17	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
18	
19	
20	def digest_text(text: str) -> str:
21	    """SHA-256 of a raw UTF-8 text payload."""
22	    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
23	
24	
25	def step(
26	    number: int,
27	    name: str,
28	    params: dict[str, Any],
29	    input_sha256: str,
30	    output_sha256: str,
31	    previous_sha256: str | None,
32	) -> dict[str, Any]:
33	    """Build one provenance link; its hash covers the previous link's hash."""
34	    body = {
35	        "step": number,
36	        "name": name,
37	        "params": params,
38	        "input_sha256": input_sha256,
39	        "output_sha256": output_sha256,
40	        "previous_sha256": previous_sha256,
41	    }
42	    return {**body, "hash": digest(body)}
43	
44	
45	def verify_chain(steps: Any) -> bool:
46	    """Recompute every link hash and the chain linkage."""
47	    if not isinstance(steps, list) or not steps:
48	        return False
49	    previous: str | None = None
50	    for number, entry in enumerate(steps, start=1):
51	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(STEP_FIELDS) | {"hash"}:
52	            return False
53	        if entry["step"] != number or entry["previous_sha256"] != previous:
54	            return False
55	        body = {field: entry[field] for field in STEP_FIELDS}
56	        if digest(body) != entry["hash"]:
57	            return False
58	        previous = entry["hash"]
59	    return True

60	def execute(parsed: dict[str, Any], vcf_text: str, params: dict[str, Any], lineage: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
61	    """Run ingest -> filter -> annotate -> summarize and record each link.
62	
63	    With ``lineage=True`` the result additionally carries a self-contained
64	    ``lineage`` manifest (see :mod:`variantrail.lineage`). A non-boolean
65	    ``lineage`` raises ``TypeError``; so do parameters whose values cannot be
66	    represented as JSON, and that check runs before any pipeline step.
67	    """
68	    if not isinstance(lineage, bool):
69	        raise TypeError("lineage must be a boolean")
70	    if lineage:
71	        # Validated and isolated before any step executes; later mutation of
72	        # the caller's params can never reach the returned manifest.
73	        params_snapshot = json_snapshot(params)
74	    else:
75	        params_snapshot = None
76	    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
77	    lineage_steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
78	
79	    def link(
80	        name: str,
81	        step_params: dict[str, Any],
82	        input_sha256: str,
83	        output_sha256: str,
84	    ) -> None:
85	        """Append one provenance link and, when enabled, its lineage record."""
86	        steps.append(
87	            step(
88	                len(steps) + 1,
89	                name,
90	                step_params,
91	                input_sha256,
92	                output_sha256,
93	                None if not steps else steps[-1]["hash"],
94	            )
95	        )
96	        if lineage:
97	            previous_sha256 = GENESIS_SHA256 if not lineage_steps else lineage_steps[-1]["sha256"]
98	            lineage_steps.append(
99	                lineage_record(
100	                    name,
101	                    json_snapshot(step_params),
102	                    input_sha256,
103	                    output_sha256,
104	                    previous_sha256,
105	                )
106	            )
107	
108	    records = parsed["records"]
109	    link(
110	        "ingest",
111	        {"parser_version": PARSER_VERSION},
112	        digest_text(vcf_text),
113	        digest({"records": records}),
114	    )
115	
116	    reasons = list(RECORD_FILTER_REASONS)
117	    expression = params.get("record_filter")
118	    if expression is not None:
119	        reasons.append(RULE_MISMATCH)
120	    counts = dict.fromkeys(reasons, 0)
121	    kept: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
122	    for record in records:
123	        reason = record_reason(record, params)
124	        if reason is None:
125	            kept.append(record)
126	        else:
127	            counts[reason] += 1
128	    filter_params: dict[str, Any] = {
129	        "min_dp": params["min_dp"],
130	        "min_qual": params["min_qual"],
131	        "pass_only": params["pass_only"],
132	    }
133	    if expression is not None:
134	        filter_params["record_filter"] = expression
135	    link(
136	        "filter",
137	        filter_params,
138	        steps[-1]["output_sha256"],
139	        digest({"filter_counts": counts, "records": kept}),
140	    )
141	
142	    variants: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
143	    filtered = 0
144	    for record in kept:
145	        annotations = [entry for entry in annotate(record) if allele_selected(entry, params)]
146	        if not annotations:
147	            filtered += 1
148	            continue
149	        variants.append(variant_document(record, annotations))
150	    counts = {**counts, "allele_filtered": filtered}
151	    link(
152	        "annotate",
153	        {
154	            "annotation_table_sha256": table_sha256(),
155	            "genes": params["genes"],
156	            "impacts": params["impacts"],
157	        },
158	        steps[-1]["output_sha256"],
159	        digest({"filter_counts": counts, "variants": variants}),
160	    )
161	
162	    statistics = summarize(records, variants, counts)
163	    link("summarize", {}, steps[-1]["output_sha256"], digest(statistics))
164	
165	    result: dict[str, Any] = {
166	        "filter_counts": counts,
167	        "provenance": steps,
168	        "statistics": statistics,
169	        "variants": variants,
170	    }
171	    if lineage:
172	        result["lineage"] = build_manifest(vcf_text, params_snapshot, lineage_steps)
173	    return result

176	def record_reason(record: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
177	    """First failing record-level filter, in the documented precedence order."""
178	    if params["pass_only"] and record["filter"] != ["PASS"]:
179	        return "not_pass"
180	    if record["qual"] is None:
181	        if params["min_qual"] > 0:
182	            return "qual_below_min"
183	    elif record["qual"] < params["min_qual"]:
184	        return "qual_below_min"
185	    if record["dp"] is None:
186	        if params["min_dp"] > 0:
187	            return "dp_below_min"
188	    elif record["dp"] < params["min_dp"]:
189	        return "dp_below_min"
190	    expression = params.get("record_filter")
191	    if expression is not None and not evaluate_record_filter(expression, record):
192	        return RULE_MISMATCH
193	    return None
194	
195	
196	def allele_selected(annotation: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
197	    """Allele-level allowlists, applied after annotation."""
198	    if params["genes"] and annotation["gene"] not in params["genes"]:
199	        return False
200	    if params["impacts"] and annotation["impact"] not in params["impacts"]:
201	        return False
202	    return True
203	
204	
205	def variant_document(record: dict[str, Any], annotations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
206	    return {
207	        "alts": list(record["alts"]),
208	        "annotations": annotations,
209	        "chrom": record["chrom"],
210	        "dp": record["dp"],
211	        "filter": list(record["filter"]),
212	        "id": record["id"],
213	        "info": dict(record["info"]),
214	        "line": record["line"],
215	        "pos": record["pos"],
216	        "qual": record["qual"],
217	        "raw": record["raw"],
218	        "ref": record["ref"],
219	    }
220	
221	
222	def summarize(
223	    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
224	    variants: list[dict[str, Any]],
225	    counts: dict[str, int],
226	) -> dict[str, Any]:
227	    consequence_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
228	    gene_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
229	    impact_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
230	    alleles_kept = 0
231	    for variant in variants:
232	        for annotation in variant["annotations"]:
233	            alleles_kept += 1
234	            _bump(consequence_counts, annotation["consequence"])
235	            _bump(gene_counts, annotation["gene"] or "NA")
236	            _bump(impact_counts, annotation["impact"])
237	    return {
238	        "alleles_kept": alleles_kept,
239	        "alleles_total": sum(len(record["alts"]) for record in records),
240	        "consequence_counts": _ordered(consequence_counts),
241	        "filter_counts": _ordered(counts),
242	        "gene_counts": _ordered(gene_counts),
243	        "impact_counts": _ordered(impact_counts),
244	        "records_filtered": len(records) - len(variants),
245	        "records_kept": len(variants),
246	        "records_total": len(records),
247	    }
248	
249	
250	def _bump(counts: dict[str, int], key: str) -> None:
251	    counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
252	
253	
254	def _ordered(counts: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
255	    return {key: counts[key] for key in sorted(counts)}
